current_status.stage: Once-monthly SC depot of ASC30 completed a U.S. Phase II 24-week study (positive topline Jun 2026); once-monthly injectable amylin agonist ASC36 and the ASC36_35 co-formulation in U.S. Phase I since Aug 2026; once-monthly triple agonist ASC37 selected for clinical development. The oral ASC30 tablet (Phase III AURORA program) and oral ASC36 (Phase I) are outside the tracker's long-acting scope.
current_status.stage_evidence: Stage follows the long-acting assets only: the once-monthly SC depot of ASC30 completed a U.S. Phase II 24-week study with positive topline results (Ascletis release, Jun 1 2026). The Phase III AURORA trials are for the once-daily oral tablet, which is out of scope.
current_status.molecule_evidence: Two assets in one umbrella: ASC30 is a small-molecule GLP-1 agonist with an ultra-long-acting SC depot, and ASC36 is a once-monthly injectable amylin receptor agonist that began Phase 1 in Aug 2026. ASC37, a once-monthly SC GLP-1R/GIPR/GCGR triple peptide agonist selected for clinical development (Ascletis press releases, 2026), also sits in other_incretin (alias added 2026-09-14 by admin).
current_status.dosing_target: Once-monthly SC depot for ASC30, with once-quarterly maintenance under study; once-monthly SC for ASC36 and ASC37
current_status.data_point: SC depot Phase II (n=65, 24 weeks): Formulation A1, three monthly 400 mg doses with no weekly lead-in, gave placebo-adjusted weight loss of 7.5% at week 16 and 5.8% at week 24. Phase Ib: observed half-life of about 75 days after a single 100 mg SC dose.

finding_history.summary: Ascletis announced positive topline results from a U.S. Phase II, 24-week study of its ultra-long-acting subcutaneous depot formulations of ASC30 (a small-molecule GLP-1R agonist, not a peptide) for obesity. Formulation A1, given as three monthly 400mg doses with no weekly lead-in injections, produced placebo-adjusted weight loss of 6.3% at week 12, 7.5% at week 16, and durable 5.8% at week 24 (16 weeks after the last dose); Formulation A2 failed to achieve therapeutic exposure. No discontinuations due to adverse events were reported.

source.name: Ascletis press release via PR Newswire

finding_history.summary: Ascletis initiated two U.S. Phase I studies for ASC36 (a once-monthly, injectable amylin receptor peptide agonist discovered via its AI-assisted structure-based drug discovery platform) and ASC36_35FDC, a fixed-dose co-formulation of ASC36 with GLP-1R/GIPR dual agonist ASC35, following FDA IND clearance. Preclinical head-to-head DIO rat data showed ASC36 monotherapy produced ~91% and ~32% greater relative body-weight reduction than petrelintide and eloralintide, respectively.

source.name: Ascletis press release via PR Newswire

finding_history.summary: Ascletis announced dosing of the first participant in its global Phase III clinical program (two pivotal trials, AURORA-1 and AURORA-2) for once-daily oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist ASC30 in chronic weight management, enrolling ~4,600 adults with obesity/overweight (with and without type 2 diabetes) over 72 weeks. Topline data expected Q3 2028; U.S. NDA submission expected by end of 2028, EU MAA submission expected early 2029.

source.name: Ascletis press release via PR Newswire

finding_history.summary: Ascletis' ultra-long-acting subcutaneous depot maintenance formulation of ASC30 (Phase Ib study NCT06679959) demonstrated an observed half-life of 75 days in participants with obesity -- after a single 100mg SC dose in 8 participants, median Tmax was 17 days and time to 50% of Cmax was ~75 days -- supporting a once-quarterly maintenance dosing regimen built on Ascletis' Ultra-Long-Acting Platform (ULAP). This Phase Ib readout predates and underlies the later Phase II 24-week topline already in this file (f-2026-06-01-001).

source.name: Ascletis press release via PR Newswire, corroborated by Clinical Trials Arena

finding_history.verification_note: Logged in September 2026, a year after publication; not picked up when it was released.

finding_history.summary: Ascletis initiated a U.S. Phase I study for ASC36 oral tablets in obesity, its fourth Phase I start of 2026 and distinct from the two injectable ASC36 studies begun in August. The oral formulation uses the company POTENT oral-transport technology, reporting 6-8% absolute oral bioavailability at steady state and up to 13.2% mean body-weight reduction from baseline after seven days of once-daily dosing in non-human primates.

source.name: Ascletis company release via PR Newswire
